newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL- Japan trade surplus to continue rise in June.
newsitem.headline: POLL- Japan trade surplus to continue rise in June.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus is expected to show a year-on-year rise in June for the third straight month as the yen's weakness earlier in May still continues to boost Tokyo's exports, economists said on Tuesday.

Economists' forecasts for the June trade surplus ranged from 971.0 billion yen to 1.61 trillion yen, or a rise of between 33 percent and 120 percent from the surplus of 731.6 billion yen in June 1996.
The data will be announced at 8.50 a.m. on Thursday (2350 GMT Wednesday).
"The yen's weakness back in early May is still having an effect. It has pushed up exports while capping imports," said Yoshiteru Hoshi, an economist at DKB Research Institute.
The yen fell to around 127.45 yen to the dollar on May 1, its lowest level since August 1992.
Hoshi added that Japanese exports were likely to show a year-on-year increase of 18.5 percent in June, marking the third straight month of a rise above 10 percent.
Economists also said healthy economic growth overseas, especially in the United States, had led to strong Japanese exports.
"Car exports in particular are very strong, led by those to the U.S.," Daiwa Bank Research said in a report.

The drop in domestic demand following a rise in the consumption tax in April resulted in a decrease of imports while encouraging Japanese manufacturers to boost their exports to make up for the drop in consumption back home, economists also said.
Japan raised its consumption tax to five percent from three on April 1.

Although the magnitude of the rise in June was likely to be smaller than that in May, when the trade surplus rose by 222.2 percent from a year earlier, economists said the rising trend was likely to continue for some time.
CS First Boston said in a report that the surplus was likely to expand beyond June and it would take several months for the pace of the year-on-year rise to slow to single digit growth.

"The surplus will continue to rise gradually during the current fiscal year if the dollar/yen rate remains at the current level of around 112 to 113 yen to a dollar," said DKB Research's Hoshi, adding that at this level, Japanese exporting firms will be able to raise profits.
Forecasts by individual research firms are as follows:
NCB RESEARCH INSTITUTE 971.0 billion yen
DKB RESEARCH INSTITUTE 1.01 trillion yen
DAIWA BANK RESEARCH 1.01 trillion yen
YAMAICHI RESEARCH INSTITUTE 1.13 trillion yen
NOMURA RESEARCH INSTITUTE 1.16 trillion yen
INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN 1.22 trillion yen
MERRILL LYNCH JAPAN 1.35 trillion yen
KANKAKU RESEARCH INSTITUTE 1.58 trillion yen
CS FIRST BOSTON 1.61 trillion yen
